newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin would ask Renault to keep plant open - Monde.
newsitem.headline: Jospin would ask Renault to keep plant open - Monde.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin would ask Renault SA to look for ways to keep the doomed Vilvoorde plant open if the Socialists won Sunday's elections, the newspaper Le Monde said on Saturday.
Citing a statement by the European Parliament's Socialists, Le Monde said Jospin made the commitment in Lille on Thursday.

Renault announced in February that it planned to close the Belgian plant this year to streamline its European car assembly operations. The French state is Renault's largest shareholder, holding 46 percent after share sales in 1994 and last year.

"The state's representatives on the board would ask that other measures be envisaged, studied and prepared to resolve the problems of production costs at the Vilvoorde plant," Jospin was quoted as saying.
Renault has said only Chairman Louis Schweitzer, onetime chief of staff of former Socialist Prime Minister Laurent Fabius, can go back on the decision.

Schweitzer has said the decision is irrevocable and essential to the efficient running of the assembly plant network. Renault, the smallest of Europe's full-range carmakers, lost 5.25 billion francs ($911.8 million) last year, including 3.9 billion in restructuring charges, in a fiercely competitive environment.
The state has five representatives on the 15-member board, and the company's employees have three.
Renault's unions say they will be in a better position to stop the closure if the Socialists beat the ruling centre-right RPR-UDP coalition in the parliamentary election runoff.

Renault announced earlier this month that it would meet representatives of the European staff on June 3 after French and Belgian courts ruled it could not close the plant until it met with the European staff council to discuss the shutdown.
The rulings bore on the procedure, not the decision itself to close the plant, which employs 3,100 people.
